questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted my destination to be a large city in Europe that could offer culture and social activities in the city. Furthermore, I wanted to go somewhere I had never been. 
Also I wanted to go to a university with a wide variety of courses taught in english. Prague fulfilled all that.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A bit difficult and confusing. I didn't really seem like there was a routine way of doing it from Charles University which surprised me since they have been taking international students for many years. At times it seemed as it was the first time for the university as well. A bit chaotic and not very transparent in the beginning.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Some e-mails with links to different websites explaining stuff as well as a Zoom-meeting.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It would be nice if it was a bit more streamlined and less chaotic. There was a lot of information from a lot of different sources which made it confusing. It would make it a whole lot easier if the information was coming from fewer sources and a bit more cut to the bone.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was okay. I asked around and got advice from friends of friends who had been living in Prague. They helped me find some good Facebook groups that you have to know about to find. That worked quite well for me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I loved it. Personally, I like to separate my uni life a bit from the rest of my life so that my studies and uni doesn't completely take over my life. 

But I guess for some people it can be a bit tough getting to meet new people in the beginning. So if you're going to live off campus I would definitely recommend living with other people in a shared flat or something like that. That helped me a whole lot in the beginning as they could introduce me to other people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's expensive to live off campus but on the other hand it is in most capitals in Europe.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very confusing in the start. Not much help and you kind of just had to try yourself.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was done through their online system. You had to find the courses in their catalog and then apply for them. It was easy enough once you understood how the system worked. However, the system is very old and not very intuitive.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could go to the Erasmus office and ask for help or send them an e-mail (the response time for e-mails was very long though). Mostly I asked other students or teachers.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for most of the courses I wanted to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and don't panic. In the end it will all be solved.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The general level of the academic programmes varied a lot. Some were on a high level some were not and the same goes for the teachers/students commitment to the courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some were on a high level some were not. That of course made some courses more interesting than others as it became a bit boring in some. In some of the courses I took, the teacher did not expect a whole lot from the students, which almost deactivated people so they only delivered the bare minimum.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. I'm used to more lectures in auditoriums and then when we do class courses at UCPH the teachers normally demand more active participation from the students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Science Fiction for he Moment 

Modernism and Modernity 

Contemporary Poetry and Poetics

American and Canadian Literature: Civil War to WWII

What is an Image? Philosophical Reflections

Introduction to Scandinavian Film

English. Exploring Art and Visual Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Modernism and Modernity 

Contemporary Poetry and Poetics

These two coursed I really enjoyed and learned a lot from. They were challenging but in the end I really feel like a learned a lot. Also it was a small amount of students that attended these courses which made it possible to be very active in class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Buying groceries were a bit more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't look into that so I don't know.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different parties and social stuff arranged by the ESN.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't do a lot of activities through uni. I mostly did stuff with friends outside of uni.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Charles Bridge, The Clock Tower and all bars because the beers are so cheap. It's like Berlin but just cheaper.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fine. Not that different from my home country.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's a bit difficult getting to local students as they mostly stick to themselves which I understand. I don't really know just try to talk to them and be nice I guess.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that people had so many different classes so you never really got to know people from your classes which is different from what I'm used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I think the Czech people are very direct and honest which makes it a lot easier to get to know people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try out new courses that are different from what you normally study - it's a good opportunity to try out other subjects. 

Try to grab coffee or lunch with the people from your classes. It's nice getting to know your fellow students which can also make boring classes more fun to attend to. 

Don't spend too much time stressing about the courses and make the most out of the new city you've just arrived in.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't let the slightly chaotic beginning stress you out too much and just have a good time. All the courses and different stuff will be solved and the employees are very friendly, helpfull and flexible.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing that you can go to a different city in a different country where you don't know a single person, and then in only half a year you can build up an entire life with friends and a connection to the city. That was a very motivating experience for me.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Saying goodbye to people leaving in the end. It's difficult because people are from all over the world so all of the sudden you can't see each other that often.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
